QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_18

question.text: Difference-in-Differences (DiD) is MOST appropriate when the SIA:

answer.text: Wants to build a Logic Model for a new program
Has only end-line qualitative narratives from five beneficiaries
Has baseline and end-line data for both a treatment group and a comparison group not randomly assigned but presumed to follow the same secular trend absent the intervention
Needs to monetise outcomes for an SROI ratio

explanation.text: The Logic: DiD compares the change (delta) in outcome for the treated group to the change for a comparison group over the same period. Its identifying assumption is 'parallel trends' — the two groups would have evolved similarly absent the intervention. It requires pre- and post-intervention data for BOTH groups. The Trap: Qualitative narratives support triangulation, not DiD. Logic Model is a planning tool, not an evaluation technique. Monetisation is the SROI step after causal evidence is established. Cross-Exam Context: XV Research Analyst and policy-research syllabi reference DiD in natural-experiment case studies. XXIII applies it to SIA quasi-experimental design. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Always plot pre-period trends for treated vs comparison group before applying DiD — if the lines diverge pre-intervention, parallel-trends fails and you must switch to synthetic control or propensity score matching.
